action.rationale: Fresh problem (dim=10) with a modest total budget of 100; per our policy we first learn the landscape. Probing ~12% of the budget is inexpensive on a cheap, deterministic objective and will guide the choice between global and local methods.

Probes indicate a moderately funnelled but not clearly single-basin landscape (P2 fdc_spearman=0.5315, top10_spread_over_diag=0.3515) with substantial variation (P1 log10_range=2.066). In 10D with cheap, deterministic evals and 88 left, a small race between CMA-ES and TuRBO efficiently selects the better driver before committing more budget.

TuRBO won the race decisively (114.86 vs 139.76) and is now active with evals_in_tenure=0 and tr_length=0.8, so it hasn’t had a full run yet. With 58 evals left on a cheap, deterministic 10D problem, continuing TuRBO should yield further improvement before polishing.

Only 8 evals remain (92/100 used) and Turbo is still making progress (best 83.08 → 82.05 over the last 9 evals; stall_evals=1) with tr_length=0.4 and not exhausted. With 10D, polishers like BOBYQA/Nelder–Mead would be starved for points, so continuing Turbo is the safest way to squeeze marginal gains.
